dialogue.origin: （こんばんは。本日はよろしくお願い致します。お時間になりましたら始めさせていただきますね。）
dialogue.content: (Good evening. Thank you for working with me today. We'll begin when it's time.)

dialogue.origin: こんばんは。相談員です。本日は、ご相談に来てくださりありがとうございます。はじめに、年齢、性別、ご相談内容を教えていただけますか？
dialogue.content: Good evening. I am the counselor. Thank you for coming for a consultation today. To begin, could you please tell me your age, gender, and what you would like to discuss?

dialogue.origin: こんばんわ。宜しくお願いします。22歳男友達の件で相談があります。
dialogue.content: Good evening. Nice to meet you. I'm a 22-year-old man, and I'd like to talk about a friend of mine.

dialogue.origin: 教えてくださりありがとうございます。お友達のことでご相談なのですね。
dialogue.content: Thank you for sharing that. So you'd like to discuss something about your friend.

dialogue.origin: お友達と何かございましたか？
dialogue.content: Did something happen with your friend?

dialogue.origin: はい、最近のことですが、高校時代のメンバーで飲み会があったんです。
dialogue.content: Yes, recently we had a drinking get-together with my high school friends.

dialogue.origin: そこで昔から合わないなって感じている子も来ていて
dialogue.content: Someone I’ve never really gotten along with was there, too.

dialogue.origin: そうなのですね。続けてお話し下さいね。
dialogue.content: I see. Please go on.

dialogue.origin: 最初からこの子が来ると言うのは聞いてたのですが、遅れてくるので来たら帰ろうと考えてたんです
dialogue.content: I knew from the start that this person was coming, but since they were going to be late, I was planning to leave when they arrived.

dialogue.origin: いざ来て帰ろうとして用件つけて帰ろうとしたのですが他の仲のいい友達にいとくようにお願いされていたのですが
dialogue.content: When they actually arrived, I tried to make an excuse to leave, but my other close friends had asked me to stay.

dialogue.origin: やっぱり言う事がちょいちょい腹が立つことばかりで
dialogue.content: But as expected, they kept saying little things that really irritated me.

dialogue.origin: 場を崩したくなくて帰れず
dialogue.content: I didn't want to ruin the atmosphere, so I couldn't leave.

dialogue.origin: そうなのですね。色々とご自分なりに考えて、何とか帰ろうとしてはみたもの、場を崩したくなく、帰れなかったのですね。
dialogue.content: I see. So you thought it over and tried to find a way to leave, but you couldn't because you didn't want to ruin the mood.

dialogue.origin: 場所を変えて2次会にもう限界で何も言わずに帰ったんのは帰ったのですがずっとイライラがおさまらなくて、
dialogue.content: We moved to another place for the after-party, and I was at my limit, so I just left without saying anything. But I've been irritated ever since, and it won't go away.

dialogue.origin: そうなんです！
dialogue.content: Exactly!

dialogue.origin: そうだったのですね。やっと帰ることができたものの、帰ってからイライラがおさまらないくらいおつらい気持ちだったのですね。
dialogue.content: I see. So even though you finally managed to leave, you've been feeling so upset that the irritation hasn't gone away.

dialogue.origin: 以前まではできるだけ近くに行かないように話も避けてはいたのですが、今回流れで一緒に飲むことになってしまって
dialogue.content: Until now, I had avoided talking to them and tried not to get too close, but this time, things just led to us drinking together.

dialogue.origin: なるほど。今までは上手く一緒にならないようにできていたのですね。でも今回は避けられなかったのですね。
dialogue.content: I see. So until now, you had been able to successfully avoid being with them. But this time it was unavoidable.

dialogue.origin: 帰った後は好きな友達にも迷惑かけたし、その合わない子が悪口みたいなように伝えたみたいで
dialogue.content: After I left, I feel like I caused trouble for the friends I like, and it seems that the person I don’t get along with told them things that sounded like they were bad-mouthing me.

dialogue.origin: 好きな友達にも自分が悪いような雰囲気なんです
dialogue.content: Now, even with the friends I like, it feels like I’m the one at fault.

dialogue.origin: そうだったのですね。仲の良い好きなお友達に対しても自分が悪いように思われてしまっている感じなのですね。
dialogue.content: I see. So you feel that even your good, close friends think you are at fault.

dialogue.origin: はい、、
dialogue.content: Yes...

dialogue.origin: それは、帰ってからのイライラに加え、とてもショックな気持ちですよね。
dialogue.content: On top of the irritation after getting home, that must have been quite a shock.

dialogue.origin: 仲の良いお友達は、あなたの気持ちを理解してくれている感じはないのでしょうか？
dialogue.content: Do you feel that your close friends don't understand your feelings?

dialogue.origin: はい、元はと言えばこの人のせいで帰ったのにあることないこと友達に話してたみたいで
dialogue.content: Yes. I left because of this person in the first place, but it seems they told our friends all sorts of things, whether true or not.

dialogue.origin: そうですね、
dialogue.content: That's right.

dialogue.origin: 友達誰1人僕がこの人避けてるようにしてるの言ってないし気づかせないようにしてるので
dialogue.content: I haven't told a single friend that I'm avoiding this person, and I've been trying to act so they won't notice.

dialogue.origin: そうなのですね。それは、とても腹立だしい気持ちにもなりますね。また、あなたは気を遣って仲良しのお友達に気づかれないように接していたのですね。
dialogue.content: I see. That must be very frustrating. And you were being considerate, acting in a way that your close friends wouldn't notice.

dialogue.origin: そうです！この人のこと嫌いって人はあまりいないではあるので
dialogue.content: Exactly! And not many people seem to dislike this person.

dialogue.origin: 仲の良いお友達に気遣っていたあなたの思いやりが伝わってきます。でも、苦手なお友達に色々とかき乱されて、とても嫌な気持ちになっているのですね。
dialogue.content: I can see your thoughtfulness in being considerate of your close friends. But this person you struggle with stirred things up and left you feeling very upset.

dialogue.origin: 仕事とかではないプライベートの飲みの場は気を遣ったり好きじゃない人とは飲みたくないので
dialogue.content: At a private get-together that's not for work, I don't want to have to be on guard or drink with people I don't like.

dialogue.origin: そうなのですね。あなたの中で、そう思って飲み会を楽しむことにしているのですね。
dialogue.content: I understand. So for you, that's the mindset you have in order to enjoy these get-togethers.

dialogue.origin: そうなんです。全然ケンカでどうにかしようと思えばできるのですが、飲みの場でそんな事したくないし
dialogue.content: That's right. I could totally try to settle things with a fight if I wanted, but I don't want to do that at a get-together.

dialogue.origin: あっちがよくケンカうってくるのでやってもいいけどって感じに毎回なるんですが
dialogue.content: They often try to pick a fight with me, so every time I end up feeling like, "Fine, let's do this," but...

dialogue.origin: 酒癖悪い子で
dialogue.content: They're a nasty drunk.

dialogue.origin: あなたの苦手な方のことを嫌いという人はあまりいないそうですが、あなたはその方のケンカをすぐ売ってくるところや、酒癖の悪いところが嫌なのですね？
dialogue.content: You said that not many people dislike the person you struggle with, but you dislike how they are quick to pick a fight and are a nasty drunk. Is that correct?

dialogue.origin: 高校の時に何回かケンカみたいになっててそれで皆んなとは違う態度だから嫌いの人はいないのかなとは思いますが
dialogue.content: We got into a few fights in high school, and I think maybe no one else dislikes them because their attitude is different when they're with everyone else.

dialogue.origin: そうなのですね。高校時代にそのようなことがあってからなのですね。
dialogue.content: I see. So this has been going on since those incidents in high school.

dialogue.origin: んーもともと性格が高校で会った時から合わなくて共通の会話がないから
dialogue.content: Hmm, well, our personalities haven't matched since we first met in high school, and we have nothing in common to talk about.

dialogue.origin: 嫌いとかではないけど絡まないって感じでした
dialogue.content: It wasn't that I disliked them; it was more that I just didn't interact with them.

dialogue.origin: そうなのですね。性格が合わないって事はあって当然ですよね。でも、あなたはケンカはしたくないので上手く交わしてきたのですね。とても、大人の対応だと私は思います。
dialogue.content: I understand. It’s perfectly natural that some personalities don’t match. But you didn’t want to fight, so you’ve been skillfully deflecting them. I think that’s a very mature way to handle it.

dialogue.origin: 家に帰ってからイライラがおさまらなかった一番の原因は何でしょうか？
dialogue.content: What would you say was the main reason your irritation wouldn't go away after you got home?

dialogue.origin: プライベートで2人でしたらいいとは思いますが、高校時代全国大会で戦っててとっても仲のいいチームなんで、今でも全国決まった日に父母も選手も飲み会するので
dialogue.content: If it were just the two of us in private, I think it would be fine, but we were a really close team in high school that competed in the national championships. Even now, the players and our parents have a get-together on the anniversary of when we qualified for nationals.

dialogue.origin: そうなのですね。そういう流れがあっての飲み会だったのですね。
dialogue.content: I see. So that was the context for this get-together.

dialogue.origin: 出来れば周りにもこの子にもわからないままの方が面倒にならないかなって思ってこんな決断を取っていて、、
dialogue.content: I figured it would be less trouble if neither my other friends nor this person noticed, so I’ve been making my decisions based on that...

dialogue.origin: やっぱり本人と話すべきでしょうか？
dialogue.content: Should I talk to them directly after all?

dialogue.origin: 仲の良いチームだったので、できれば場をこわしたくないし、面倒なことにしたくない気持ちが強いのですね。
dialogue.content: Because it was such a close team, you have a strong desire not to ruin the atmosphere or cause any trouble.

dialogue.origin: そうです！
dialogue.content: Exactly!

dialogue.origin: 仮に本人と話をするとしたら、どのような内容をお話したいと思いますか？
dialogue.content: If you were to talk to them, what sort of things would you want to say?

dialogue.origin: んー
dialogue.content: Hmm...

dialogue.origin: 嫌いではないけどー
dialogue.content: "It's not that I dislike you, but..."

dialogue.origin: 腹立つところがあるとかでしょうか？
dialogue.content: "...there are things about you that irritate me?" Something like that?

dialogue.origin: あなたは、仲の良いチームを大切に思われているようですので、できれば気の合わない子とも今よりは話をしたいと思いますか？
dialogue.content: It seems you truly treasure your close team, so would you ideally like to be able to talk with this person you don't get along with more than you do now?

dialogue.origin: この前にこの子と話してないのに友だちの話の中に入ってきてガキかお前って言われたんですが
dialogue.content: The other day, I wasn't even talking to them, but they butted into a conversation with my friends and said to me, "Are you a kid or what?"

dialogue.origin: いやいや、わざわざこの歳になってまだ歯向かってくるあなたの方がガキと思いますがとかですかね
dialogue.content: I might say something like, "No, no, I think the one who's still trying to pick fights at this age is the real kid."

dialogue.origin: 現に高校の時から性格合わないから一度たりともあなたに話しかけた事ない大人の対応したと思いますがって感じですかね
dialogue.content: Or maybe, "The fact is, our personalities haven't matched since high school, so I think I've been very mature by never once starting a conversation with you."

dialogue.origin: 会話が合わないというのは、今のような会話が繰り広げられるからのですね。
dialogue.content: So when you say your personalities don't match, it's because conversations like the one you just described tend to happen.

dialogue.origin: それは全くありません、、チームで集まっても話さず行きたいと思ってます
dialogue.content: Not at all. I'd rather not talk to them, even when we get together as a team.

dialogue.origin: そうですね笑あなたと話してないですが、、ってその時はなりました、
dialogue.content: That's right. (laughs) At the time, my reaction was just, "...but I'm not talking to you."

dialogue.origin: そうなのですね。話をしたいわけではないことはハッキリされているのですね。では、仮に本人と話をしたとして会話が成り立つのでしょうか？
dialogue.content: I see. So you're very clear that you don't want to talk to them. In that case, if you were to speak to them, would a constructive conversation even be possible?

dialogue.origin: んーー
dialogue.content: Hmm...

dialogue.origin: ケンカしようみたいに言われるかもですね！
dialogue.content: They might just say something like, "Are you trying to start a fight?"

dialogue.origin: なるほど。そうなんですね。あなたが話をしたいと思っても話にならなければ難しいですよね？
dialogue.content: I see. That makes sense. Even if you wanted to talk, it would be difficult if it doesn't lead to a real conversation, wouldn't it?

dialogue.origin: たしかに！
dialogue.content: That's true!

dialogue.origin: その解決方法が難しいことはわかりましたので、他の方法を考えてみましょうか？
dialogue.content: Since that approach seems difficult, shall we consider other options?

dialogue.origin: すみません、宜しくお願いします
dialogue.content: Yes, please. Thank you.

dialogue.origin: もう一度、確認なのですが、あなたはその子とは話さずに無難に仲の良いチームとの飲み会を終えれることを望んでるのですよね？
dialogue.content: Let me just confirm. You're hoping to get through the get-togethers with your close team without incident, and without having to talk to that person, correct?

dialogue.origin: そうです！
dialogue.content: That's exactly right!

dialogue.origin: でも、仲の良い友達とは楽しく飲みたいのですよね。
dialogue.content: But you want to enjoy drinking with your close friends, right?

dialogue.origin: 1次会までは大勢いるので全く会話ないのでしのげてたのしめます！
dialogue.content: At the first party, there are a lot of people so we don't talk at all. I can manage and enjoy myself!

dialogue.origin: 2次会3次会なって人数が減ってきてその子がいたら帰ると言う感じです
dialogue.content: When it gets to the second and third after-parties, the group gets smaller, and if that person is there, I leave.

dialogue.origin: そうなのですね。一次会で帰れたら何とかなるのですね？
dialogue.content: I see. So if you can leave after the first party, it's manageable?

dialogue.origin: 今回のように帰れないときが問題なのですね？
dialogue.content: The problem is when you can't leave, like what happened this time?

dialogue.origin: はい！このままにしといた方がいいですよね？
dialogue.content: Yes! So it's better to just leave things as they are, right?

dialogue.origin: でも、あなたは本当は二次会も三次会も参加したいのでしょうか？
dialogue.content: But do you actually want to join the second and third after-parties as well?

dialogue.origin: 今回のがわかったからもう断固拒否するようにしたらいいですかね？
dialogue.content: Given what happened this time, should I just firmly refuse from now on?

dialogue.origin: 参加はしたいではありますね笑
dialogue.content: I do want to participate, though. (laughs)

dialogue.origin: いつ僕も我慢できなくなって場の雰囲気壊してしまうか分からなくなってしまったので前回で
dialogue.content: After what happened last time, I don't know when I might lose my patience and ruin the atmosphere.

dialogue.origin: あなたが我慢することで、嫌な気持ちにならないで済むことを選ぶのか？我慢せずに二次会や三次会を楽しみたいのか？ですね。どちらの気持ちが強いのでしょうか？
dialogue.content: So, it's a choice between enduring it to avoid these unpleasant feelings, or not enduring it and enjoying the after-parties. Which of those feelings is stronger?

dialogue.origin: あー、難しいですね
dialogue.content: Ah, that's a tough one.

dialogue.origin: でも、我慢せずにあなたが楽しむと場の雰囲気を壊してしまう気がして悩んでいるのですね？
dialogue.content: But you're worried that if you enjoy yourself without holding back, you might ruin the atmosphere?

dialogue.origin: 我慢するなら帰りたい、
dialogue.content: If I have to endure it, I'd rather just go home.

dialogue.origin: では、質問を変えますね。あなたが一番優先させたいこと、大切にしたいことは何ですか？
dialogue.content: Then let me ask a different question. What is your top priority? What is it that you want to value the most?

dialogue.origin: 大切にしたいのは特別なチームなので雰囲気を壊したくないしこれからもこんなチームみんなで語り合う場は残したいです
dialogue.content: What I want to value most is this special team, so I don't want to ruin the atmosphere, and I want to preserve these opportunities for all of us to get together and talk in the future.

dialogue.origin: そうなのですね。あなたがチームを大切に思う気持ちがとても伝わってきます。だからこそ、尚更悩んでいるのですね。
dialogue.content: I see. I can really feel how much you value your team. That must be why you're struggling with this so much.

dialogue.origin: すみません、こんなことで。
dialogue.content: I’m sorry to bother you with something like this.

dialogue.origin: いえ。いえ、とても大切な事で悩まれていると思います。大切な仲間のことですから。では、望む形としては、雰囲気を壊さずに、このような会をずっと続けていきたいということですね。
dialogue.content: Not at all. I think this is a very important thing to be concerned about, because it's about your precious teammates. So, your desired outcome is to be able to continue these get-togethers for a long time without ruining the atmosphere, is that right?

dialogue.origin: ありがとうございます。はい！
dialogue.content: Thank you. Yes!

dialogue.origin: そうなると、はやり、誰一人欠けることなくチームで楽しめることが良いのだと、あなたの話を聴いていて思いました。
dialogue.content: In that case, listening to you, I feel the ideal would be for the whole team to be able to enjoy themselves, with no one missing.

dialogue.origin: そうですね、その子が好きな仲間もいると思うので
dialogue.content: That's right. There are probably teammates who like that person, too.

dialogue.origin: なので、チームがみんなで楽しめる時間を確保でき、あなたも我慢をしてつらい思いをすることを避けれる方法が一番ですよね。
dialogue.content: So, the best method would be one that allows the whole team to enjoy their time together, while also allowing you to avoid having to endure it and feel upset.

dialogue.origin: 周囲のことをしっかり考えているあなたは素晴らしいですね。その子が好きな仲間もいると思ってらっしゃる気持ちも、間接的にはその子への思いやりでもあると思います。
dialogue.content: It's wonderful that you think so carefully about those around you. The fact that you consider that some of your friends like that person is, in an indirect way, a form of consideration for that person as well.

dialogue.origin: そうですかねー、、
dialogue.content: You think so...?

dialogue.origin: 確かに嫌いではないけど絡みたくないだけではあるので
dialogue.content: It's true that I don't hate them; I just don't want to interact with them.

dialogue.origin: 同じ厳しい高校時代耐えた仲間ではあるので少しはその子にもあるかもしれません。
dialogue.content: We are teammates who endured the same tough high school days together, so maybe I do feel a little something for them in that sense.

dialogue.origin: 不快に思うことがあっても排除しない気持ちは、やはり全国大会までいった精神も関係しているのかも知れませんね。世の中には、すぐに人を排除したがる人もたくさんいます。
dialogue.content: That feeling of not wanting to exclude someone, even when they make you uncomfortable, might be related to the spirit that got your team to the national championships. There are many people in the world who are quick to exclude others.

dialogue.origin: あーたしかに。
dialogue.content: Ah, that's true.

dialogue.origin: あなたの人柄を感じます。そして、嫌いではないけれど絡みたくはない。そういうこともありますよね。
dialogue.content: I get a sense of your character. And it's not that you hate them, but you don't want to interact. That's a perfectly valid feeling to have.

dialogue.origin: そうなんです。あっちから絡んでこなければ全て問題ないけど
dialogue.content: Exactly. If they just didn't try to interact with me, there would be no problem.

dialogue.origin: なるべく絡まないように接していくことを努力してきたのですもんね。問題は、あちらからの絡みなのですね。
dialogue.content: You’ve made an effort to interact with them as little as possible. The problem is when they're the one who initiates it.

dialogue.origin: 何となく見えてきましたね。
dialogue.content: The picture is starting to become clearer now.

dialogue.origin: そうなんです。人それぞれなので合う合わないあると思うので合わないなら絡んでこなければいいのにって思います
dialogue.content: That's right. People are all different; some people click and some don’t. If we don’t click, I just wish they wouldn’t try to interact with me.

dialogue.origin: あちらは、あなたのことが苦手ではないのかも知れませんね。むしろ絡みたいのかも知れませんね。あなたは、あちらの気持ちをどう思われますか？
dialogue.content: Perhaps they don't see you as difficult. In fact, maybe they actually want to interact with you. What do you make of their feelings?

dialogue.origin: あー、そうかそうか
dialogue.content: Ah, I see, I see.

dialogue.origin: 自分が思う気持ちと、相手が思う気持ちが一致するとは限りませんのでね。恋愛と似ているかも知れませんね。
dialogue.content: How you feel and how the other person feels don't always match. It might be similar to romance in that way.

dialogue.origin: でもわざわざ、イラつかせるような見下すような発言する必要があるのかってなります
dialogue.content: But then I wonder why they feel the need to make such irritating and condescending remarks.

dialogue.origin: そうかそうか
dialogue.content: I see, I see.

dialogue.origin: そのような絡み方しかできない何かがあるのかも知れません。でも、好きでもない人に人は絡むでしょうか？どうでしょう？
dialogue.content: There might be a reason that's the only way they know how to interact. But do people usually try to interact with someone they don't like? What do you think?

dialogue.origin: そうかー、じゃあ僕が苦手だけど相手はそんなこと思ってなくてわざわざ嫌味言ってまでもからみたいのですかね？
dialogue.content: I see... So, even though I find them difficult, they don't feel the same way and want to interact with me, even if it means saying sarcastic things?

dialogue.origin: 合っているかどうかは、わかりませんが、恋愛に例えてみたら、好きな子を男子はいじめたり、いじったり、してきますよね？
dialogue.content: I can’t say for sure if this is right, but to use the romance analogy, boys sometimes tease or pick on a girl they like, don't they?

dialogue.origin: じゃあ嫌味の言葉出てきた時だけはいはいそうですねーって言って気づかせるようにしたらいいですか？
dialogue.content: So, when they say something sarcastic, should I just give a dismissive "Yeah, yeah, sure" to make them realize what they're doing?

dialogue.origin: 確かに言われてますねちょっかい出したがる
dialogue.content: That's true, people do say that boys like to tease the person they like.

dialogue.origin: もし、あなたが嫌でなければ、相手への反応を今までとは真逆にしてみてはどうでしょうか？今まではどのうような態度で返してましたか？
dialogue.content: If you're open to it, how about trying to react to them in the complete opposite way you have until now? How have you typically responded in the past?

dialogue.origin: 全て流してだけどこの前の帰った時だけ2人だったのでめっちゃ言い返しました
dialogue.content: I usually just let everything slide, but that last time when I left, it was just the two of us, so I really talked back to them.

dialogue.origin: それで相手は、悪口を言うことになったのですね？
dialogue.content: And that's what led to them bad-mouthing you?

dialogue.origin: 自分のお友達にそんな感じでしたね
dialogue.content: It seems so. They said things like that to my friends.

dialogue.origin: 次からは真逆に例えばどんな絡みがいいですか？
dialogue.content: So from next time, for example, what would be a good 'opposite' way to interact?

dialogue.origin: もしかしたらショックだったのかも知れませんね。では、流していた態度を嫌でなければ受け入れてみてはどうでしょう？
dialogue.content: Perhaps they were shocked. So, if you're willing, instead of just letting it slide, how about trying to accept it?

dialogue.origin: そうかそうか！
dialogue.content: I see, I see!

dialogue.origin: にっこり笑って、受け入れる態度をしてみてはどうでしょうか？
dialogue.content: How about trying to respond with a smile and an accepting attitude?

dialogue.origin: そうだね自分もガキだねとか言ってやろうと思ったけど
dialogue.content: Right, I was thinking of saying something like, "Yeah, I guess I'm a kid too," but...

dialogue.origin: そうじゃなくて例えばどんな感じがいいですかね？
dialogue.content: ...but not like that. For example, what would be a good way to respond?

dialogue.origin: そうですね。「そっかな、おれ、そんなにガキかな？」と返してみたらどうでしょうか？
dialogue.content: Let's see. How about responding with, "You think so? Am I really that childish?"

dialogue.origin: あー！そしたら自分が言おうとしてた言葉より柔らかくていいですね！
dialogue.content: Ah! That's much softer than what I was going to say. That's good!

dialogue.origin: それが受け入れる態度か！
dialogue.content: So that's what an accepting attitude is!

dialogue.origin: はい、あなたは決してガキではないので、ガキを認める必要はないと私は思います。
dialogue.content: Yes. You are by no means childish, so I don't think you need to admit to being so.

dialogue.origin: ありがとうございます！次そのような受け入れる態度で接してみます！
dialogue.content: Thank you! I'll try to respond with that kind of accepting attitude next time!

dialogue.origin: 今の言葉嬉しいです、、
dialogue.content: That means a lot to me...

dialogue.origin: 良かったです。試してみて、どうだったか様子をこちらにお話しにきてください。
dialogue.content: I'm glad. Please try it out, and come back and tell me how it went.

dialogue.origin: 確かに今のような返事は認めてるわけではないですね！自分のは認めてて全然別物ですね
dialogue.content: That's true, a response like that isn't the same as admitting it! My idea was to just admit it, so this is completely different.

dialogue.origin: わかりました。ありがとうございます
dialogue.content: I understand. Thank you.

dialogue.origin: ちょっとして言葉の使い方で変わるものですよね。言葉の力って不思議ですね。そろそろお時間となりました。本日は、大切なお話を聴かせていただきありがとうございました。
dialogue.content: It's amazing how a slight change in wording can make such a difference. The power of words is a fascinating thing. It looks like our time is about up. Thank you for sharing your important story with me today.

dialogue.origin: 本当ですね。ありがとうございました。また相談しにきます！
dialogue.content: It really is. Thank you very much. I'll come back to talk again!

dialogue.origin: 大切なチームを思うあなたの気持ちに私も温かい気持ちを思い出すことができました。あなたのその気持ち、いつまでも大切に過ごして欲しいと思いました。とても素敵な青春時代をすごされたこと、宝物にしてくださいね。またのお越しをお待ちしております。本日はありがとうございました。
dialogue.content: Your feelings for your precious team reminded me of a warmth in my own heart. I hope you will always cherish that feeling. Please treasure the wonderful youth you experienced. I look forward to seeing you again. Thank you for your time today.

dialogue.origin: （マッチングありがとうございました。）
dialogue.content: (Thank you for the session.)

dialogue.origin: （ありがとうございました。勉強になりました。また機会があれば宜しくお願いします。）
dialogue.content: (Thank you. It was a great learning experience. I hope we can do this again if there's another opportunity.)

dialogue.origin: （いつもと違ったパターンの相談事だったのでとても勉強になりました。また機会がございましたら是非よろしくお願い致します。では、失礼致します。）
dialogue.content: (This was a different type of consultation than usual, so it was a great learning experience for me. I would be happy to do this again if the opportunity arises. Well then, take care.)

topic.sub: 飲み会での友人とのトラブル
